 * and runs splitButtonHandler.
 * @class Neo.button.Split
 * @extends Neo.button.Base
 */

classData.comment:
/**
     * Creates the trigger button as a child this split button references in its vdom, so it renders once
     * and updates in place. A click on it runs this split button's own splitButtonHandler, never a controller
     * method of that name; a handler name in triggerButtonConfig resolves from this split button's controllers.
     * It owns the menu, in this split button's theme: the menu aligns to it, a click on it toggles the menu, and
     * a press anywhere else closes it.
     * @param {Object} config
     */
classData.description: Creates the trigger button as a child this split button references in its vdom, so it renders once and updates in place. A click on it runs this split button's own splitButtonHandler, never a controller method of that name; a handler name in triggerButtonConfig resolves from this split button's controllers. It owns the menu, in this split button's theme: the menu aligns to it, a click on it toggles the menu, and a press anywhere else closes it.

classData.comment:
/**
     * A click on the trigger button reaches this split button as well: the trigger is its child, and a DOM event
     * bubbles through a component's logical parents. That click belongs to the trigger, which opens the menu and
     * runs splitButtonHandler, so this split button runs its own handler only for a click on the main button.
     * @param {Object} data The click event data object.
     */
classData.description: A click on the trigger button reaches this split button as well: the trigger is its child, and a DOM event bubbles through a component's logical parents. That click belongs to the trigger, which opens the menu and runs splitButtonHandler, so this split button runs its own handler only for a click on the main button.
